title: Cross-team release ownership matrix and calendar (Sep 2026) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a cross-team ownership matrix for the September 2026 release window, an event-by-event rollout calendar, and the initial draft of release notes and rollback criteria. Goal is to reduce handoff ambiguity, speed on-call triage, and give PMs/ENG/CS a single source of truth for communication windows.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated deployment changes scheduled in the Sep 10–24 2026 window.
- Includes code pushes, infra config flips, model variant promotions, and console dashboard changes.
- Excludes private on-prem packages (handled by private-deployments team).

High-level release timeline (calendar):
- Sep 10: Preflight freeze starts, no non-critical merges after 12:00 PT. (Owners: Release Engineering + Platform)
- Sep 11–12: Automated integration and performance regression block runs (continuous perf job + evals). (Owners: Applied ML + Serving Runtime)
- Sep 13: Staging full smoke run, canary artifact build (Owners: Release Eng + Release Owners)
- Sep 14: Canary deploy to us-west-2 (10% traffic). Monitoring window 4 hours. (Owners: Platform Eng + SRE)
- Sep 15: Canary assessment and decision: promote or rollback. Slack channel #release-sep-2026 for rapid comms. (Owners: Release Commander)
- Sep 16–17: Regional staggered promotion (us-east-1, eu-west-1) if canary stable. (Owners: Platform Eng, Region Leads)
- Sep 18: Dedicated capacity migration window (for customers on Dedicated plan) — opt-in migrations only. (Owners: Dedicated Team)
- Sep 19: Release notes draft circulated to GTM and CS. Final edits by EOD Sep 20. (Owners: Product + Docs)
- Sep 21: Full production rollout and alert throttling window (Owners: Release Eng + SRE)
- Sep 22–24: Post-release soak, incident watch, and rolling regressions check. Postmortem start if any Sev>=2 incident occurs.

Ownership matrix (core roles):
- Release Commander: Ben Carter — single decision authority during canary assessment windows.
- Release Engineer (ops lead): Sofia Patel — preflight checklist, gating criteria, rollbacks.
- Platform Lead: Miguel Alvarez — infra scaling, region promotion, capacity.
- Serving Runtime Representative: Priya Shah — runtime performance regressions, kernel selection flags.
- Dedicated Lead: Amina Yusuf — reserved capacity changes and customer migrations.
- Product / Notes Owner: Leah Kim — collate user-facing release notes, feature callouts, and support messaging.
- Incident Liaison (on-call SRE): rotation below (see triage rotations).

Preflight checklist (to be completed before Sep 13 staging smoke):
- [ ] Merge freeze enforced and communicated (Slack + team emails).
- [ ] All release PRs have approvals and passing CI. Linked PRs: ensure build artifacts are tagged release/2026-09-x.
- [ ] Regression evals: perf, latency p95/p99, throughput vs baseline. Document anomalous runs.
- [ ] Model compatibility checks for KV cache and quantization flags.
- [ ] Canary manifest created: traffic split config, model variant mapping, fallback model mapping.
- [ ] Backup rollback artifact created and stored in stable bucket with ACLs.
- [ ] Customer-impacting changes flagged and communicated to CS (list attached).
- [ ] Playbook quick links updated in #runbooks and Confluence.

Canary window runbook (template steps):
- Start time + owner pinned in calendar (UTC).
- Validate telemetry baseline (token rates, latency, error rate).
- Run functional smoke tests: auth, tokenization, streaming, function-calls.
- Watch 3 metrics for 15 mins: error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute, p99 latency increase > 150ms, token throughput drop > 10% — if any trigger, pause and triage.
- If triage: collect traces (x-request-id), heap/gpu usage snapshots, kernel logs, and attach to Jira ticket.
- Decision gates: promote after 4 hours stable, or rollback if unresolved within 60 minutes of triage start.

Rollback criteria (minimum):
- Any customer-facing API errors > 0.5% sustained for 15 minutes.
- P99 latency regression > 200ms vs baseline for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Memory/GPU exhaustion events or kernel OOM.
- Data corruption or incorrect outputs detected in eval test-suite.

Triage rotations (on-call schedule for Sep 10–24):
- Primary SRE (week A): 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-16 — Luca Moretti
- Secondary SRE (week A): 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-16 — Anika Bose
- Primary SRE (week B): 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-24 — Jordan Lee
- Secondary SRE (week B): 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-24 — Mei Wong
Notes: Primary handles first-line triage. Secondary escalates to Release Commander if unresolved > 60 minutes.

Communications plan:
- Preflight: email to all engineering + @product on Sep 10 09:00 PT with known risk list.
- Canary: #release-sep-2026 channel active, PagerDuty routing to on-call SREs.
- Customer notices: CS will send proactive notice to customers on Dedicated and Reserved capacity on Sep 12.
- Post-release: summary and signal status to #all-hands-ops and product mailing list.

Draft release notes (first pass, to be refined by Product Notes Owner):
- New: Transparent per-route latency breakdowns in the Console (beta) — allows developers to slice p95/p99 by model and route.
- Improved: Serving runtime now defaults to lightweight KV caching for short prefixes, reducing token compute by ~8% on benchmarked workloads.
- Fix: Resolved race condition where model-variant fallback could return stale cache under high concurrency.
- Breaking: Internal config flag "enable_legacy_chunking" removed; customers using on-prem older runtimes should pin to compatible artifact.
- Known issues: Rare stream cutoffs when model logits exceed internal threshold — mitigation steps in runbook.

Post-release checks (first 72 hours):
- Verify token-rate stability and compare to baseline daily windows.
- Check customer error inbox and escalate top 3 issues.
- Run smoke evals against the nightly test-prompt set and watch for quality regressions.
- Schedule postmortem if any Sev>=2 incidents and publish within 5 business days.

Open decisions and TODOs (WIP):
- Finalize canary traffic % per region (proposal: 10% -> 30% after 4h). Owner: Platform Lead.
- Confirm Dedicated migration opt-in list (Owner: Dedicated Lead).
- Add runbook snippet for model-quantization reversion. Owner: Serving Runtime.
- Product to supply user-visible phrasing for the Console change in release notes (Owner: Leah Kim).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Perf dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/dash/release-template
- Staging smoke checklist (checklist file): Confluence:/pages/staging-smoke-checklist
- Quick rollback script: git repo infra/scripts/release-rollback.sh

If you are listed as an owner above, please sign off in the doc by adding a line: "Owner Name — signoff YYYY-MM-DD" and add any dependencies or blockers under the Open decisions section. This is an actionable living doc; expect updates as we lock the calendar.

Document history:
- 2026-08-30 Sofia Patel — initial draft and calendar proposal.
- 2026-09-02 Miguel Alvarez — added region promotion plan.
- 2026-09-05 Priya Shah — added runtime regression gates and KV cache note.
